gloss: to rush over to; to run up to

definitions.gloss: to rush over to; to run up to
definitions.explanation: To run toward someone or something, usually out of urgency, excitement, or concern. Conveys quick movement toward a specific person or place.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{母親|ははおや}に{駆|か}け{寄|よ}った。
examples.english: The child ran over to their mother.

examples.japanese: {倒|たお}れた{人|ひと}のもとに{駆|か}け{寄|よ}って{声|こえ}をかけた。
examples.english: I rushed over to the person who had collapsed and called out to them.

examples.japanese: {久|ひさ}しぶりに{祖父母|そふぼ}の{家|いえ}に{着|つ}くと、{犬|いぬ}が{尻尾|しっぽ}を{振|ふ}りながら{駆|か}け{寄|よ}ってきた。
examples.english: When I arrived at my grandparents' house after a long time, the dog came running over wagging its tail.

notes:
An intransitive godan verb composed of {駆|か}ける (to run/dash) + {寄|よ}る (to approach). The ～てくる form ({駆|か}け{寄|よ}ってくる) emphasizes someone running toward the speaker.

ASPECT (ている):
Not commonly used in the ている form since it describes a quick, punctual action.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- ～に{駆|か}け{寄|よ}る (rush over to someone/something)
- ～のもとに{駆|か}け{寄|よ}る (rush to someone's side)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {駆|か}け{寄|よ}ってくる (come running over)
- {駆|か}け{寄|よ}って{抱|だ}きつく (rush over and hug)
- {駆|か}け{寄|よ}って{声|こえ}をかける (rush over and call out)
